data.name: Hozaifah
data.gender_notes: Hozaifah is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Hozaifah is a name derived from the Arabic language, meaning 'one who fights for truth.' In Islamic history, Hozaifah ibn al-Yaman was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), known for his bravery and dedication to the faith. The name Hozaifah carries the meaning “Fighter for truth” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hozaifah usually hope their child will grow to embody fighter for truth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that inspires courage and truthfulness
data.etymology: Hozaifah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fighter for truth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hozaifah total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: حُذَيْفَة
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من حذف بمعنى قلم أو نقص
in_arabic.long_meaning: حُذَيْفَة هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه المشتق من حذف أي قلم أو نقص، و يوحي بالدقة و الحذف. و هو من الأسماء التي وردت في السيرة النبوية و التاريخ الإسلامي، حيث كان حُذَيْفَة بن بدر أو حُذَيْفَة بن اليمان من الصحابة و كان كاتب النبي محمد صلى الله عليه و سلم.

in_english.name: Hozaifah
in_english.meaning: Derived from Arabic root 'ḥ-dh-f' meaning to decrease or to wipe
in_english.long_meaning: Hozaifah is a masculine name originating from Arabic roots. It is derived from the root 'ḥ-dh-f', which means to decrease, wipe, or diminish. The name signifies precision and carefulness. Historically, it is associated with notable figures such as Huzayfah ibn Badr or Huzayfah ibn al-Yaman, companions of Prophet Muhammad and his scribes. The name reflects spiritual meanings of humility and meticulousness.

historical_references.reference: Hozaifah ibn al-Yaman was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad and took part in several battles during the early Islamic period. He is most famous for his role in the Battle of Uhud where he fought bravely and was one of the few Muslims to successfully defend the Prophet from the enemy's attack. Hozaifah's bravery was such that he continued to fight despite being wounded in both his legs.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic period, Battle of Uhud

historical_references.reference: After the Battle of Uhud, Hozaifah became a prominent figure in Medina. He was known for his piety and knowledge of Islamic law. He was also a teacher and mentor to many young Muslims. During the Ridda Wars, Hozaifah led an army against the rebel forces and played a crucial role in putting down the rebellion in the northern Arabian Peninsula.
